text: It was 3:12 every Thursday morning and Mara found the book in the bread rack. Always the same one, The Practical Guide to Inland Birds. Cracked blue spine, library stamp from a town forty miles away. She put it on the flour bin, wiped butter off the cover, meant to return it after her shift. But by noon the heat and all the errands and the sleep would eat the thought whole. Then next Thursday, same thing, it'd be tucked in there between cooling rye loaves again. Tonight the bakery hummed with the proofing cabinet and old radio static. Rain pressing silver lines down the front window. Mara lifted the book with both hands, and it felt warm. There was a receipt folded inside, marking the chapter on herons. She opened it, and in block letters someone had written I THINK YOU ARE THE ONLY PERSON AWAKE WHEN I AM. PAGE 47. She went to page 47. A grey heron stood in a marsh, one foot raised, as patient as a saint. Under the picture, in pencil, THURSDAY, 3:30? The clock over the mixer clicked once. She brushed flour off her apron, unlocked the front door, and turned on the little OPEN sign.
